findings.issue: `publisher` is set to `doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C`, the dataset's own DOI. The slot declares 'the organization or entity responsible for making the resource available'; a dataset is not its own publisher. The bundle attests University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData, UVa's Scholarly Research) as the distributing organization, and supplies ROR:0153tk833 for the University of Virginia in the June 2026 creator affiliations. Replace with the organization identifier or omit the slot.

The Dataverse citation is quoted material and must keep its source form exactly, but the record renders 'Bélisle-Pipon JC' as 'Belisle-Pipon JC' inside the citation string, and the creator entry carries the same de-accented spelling. All four Dataverse release records in the bundle write 'Bélisle-Pipon'. The American-English rule governs composed prose only, not proper nouns or quoted citations.

Both slots describe the MuSIC cell-map construction pipeline (node2vec PPI embedding, HPA image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection, GO/Reactome alignment, LLM assembly naming), sourced from the tier-3 preprint's Tools Module. The tier-1 subject release states 'Computed cell maps not included in this release' and the record itself records that limitation under `known_limitations`. As written these slots assert preprocessing applied to the distributed data that the release says it does not contain — an internal inconsistency. Either scope the entries explicitly to the project pipeline rather than to this release's contents, or omit them.

`id` on every object in the digest is declared `uriorcurie`, but the value is the bare grant number `1OT2OD032742-01`, which is neither a URI nor a CURIE with a declared prefix. The bundle supplies no identifier scheme for NIH awards; the grant number belongs in a name/label field or, if `id` must be populated, as a fragment on an attested identifier.

Byte counts are derived by decimal expansion of the Dataverse display strings ('113.3 KB' → 113300, '1.1 MB' → 1100000, '30.2 KB' → 30200). These are rounded display values presented as exact integers, and the conversion factor (1000 vs 1024) is not stated by the source. The same record omits `total_bytes` for the three image collections displayed in GB, so the slot is populated inconsistently across sibling entries. Either omit throughout or record the displayed size in prose.

The immunofluorescence instance uses B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 (Image) where the vocabulary supplied in the digest offers B2AI_SUBSTRATE:56 (Immunofluorescence Image), an exact match for what the bundle describes ('immunofluorescence-based staining (ICC-IF) and confocal microscopy'). The more specific term should be used.

`label` is `false`, yet `label_description` is populated with a description of the four fluorescence channels (DAPI, calreticulin, tubulin, protein of interest). Channel composition is not label information; the slot description asks about the label associated with an instance. This content belongs in the instance's own description or in the imaging file-collection descriptions.

Supported omission. The tier-1 October 2025 and tier-5 June 2025 release records state that each MDA-MB-468 immunofluorescence collection covers 'the spatial localization of 464 proteins of interest', and the March 2025 release states 563 for its own image sets. No per-condition protein count appears anywhere in the record, although `counts` is available on Instance and the value is attested for the image sets carried forward into this release.

Supported omission. The subject release lists a second Related Publication — Nourreddine S et al., 'A PERTURBATION CELL ATLAS OF HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS', bioRxiv 2024, doi 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, PMCID PMC11580897 — which describes the perturb-seq component distributed here. It appears nowhere in the record, while the Clark et al. preprint is represented.

`versions_available` is multivalued but holds a single prose string enumerating four prior releases with their DOIs and versions. One entry per version would represent the distinct entities the slot declares; the collapsed form also duplicates content already carried by `related_datasets`.

A single DistributionDate entry merges the current release date, the later image-file publication date, and the dates of four prior releases into one prose blob. `distribution_dates` is multivalued; distinct release events should be separate entries.

Both entries state only that ethical review 'is identified in the release record as the responsibility of named ethics leads' — a pointer to where the information sits rather than the review information itself, with the substantive content (who) already carried by `contact_person`. The bundle states no IRB number, reviewing body or determination for this release, so the details field adds nothing; `reviewing_organization` is also unpopulated.

The release names the Data Governance Committee contact as 'Jillian Parker (jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu)'. The record attaches ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486, taken from the creator listed as 'Parker J'. The bundle never equates the two forms of the name; the ORCID linkage is inferred, however plausible. The attested email is not recorded anywhere.

'University of California San Diego' as the accountable organization is inferred from the governance contact's email domain and the copyright statement naming the Regents of the University of California; the bundle does not name an accountable organization for the data over time. The release does attest that long-term preservation sits with the University of Virginia Dataverse, which the record places under `retention_limit` instead.
`language: en` is not stated anywhere in the bundle. It is a safe inference from the material but remains an unattested value under the evidence boundary.

Supported omission. The release records 'Depositor: Niestroy, Justin' with 'Deposit Date 2025-02-27'. This is currently buried in a `maintainers` entry, where the depositor role fits poorly (Maintainer.role is set to `academic_institution` for an individual); `created_by` is the fitting scalar slot.
Supported omission. All four Dataverse release records state 'Subject: Medicine, Health and Life Sciences', a classification term absent from the keyword list and from the description.

The entry describing incomplete final form and temporary pre-publication embargo is typed `integration_limitation`. Embargo and incompleteness are not integration constraints; `scope_limitation` or `temporal_limitation` fit the described condition better, and the enum offers no completeness term.

summary: Eighteen findings against the full record, one high, four medium, thirteen low. The single high-severity defect is `publisher` set to the dataset's own DOI, a value that is both semantically wrong and easily repaired from attested evidence. Medium findings concern fidelity and consistency rather than fabrication: an accented proper noun altered inside a quoted Dataverse citation; preprocessing and labeling strategies that describe cell-map construction the subject release explicitly states it does not contain; a bare grant number in a slot the digest declares `uriorcurie`; and byte counts derived by expanding rounded display strings, applied to some file collections but not others. Low findings are chiefly under-specification (a generic image substrate where an immunofluorescence term exists, channel description misplaced in `label_description`, pointer-style `review_details`), multivalued slots collapsed into single prose entries (`versions_available`, `distribution_dates`), two inferred identity or organization linkages, one unattested `language` value, and four supported omissions (per-condition protein counts, the second Related Publication, the depositor, the Dataverse subject term). No fabricated dataset facts, no enum violations, and no prior-D4D reuse were detected; the record's handling of the Sali affiliation conflict, the U2OS scope exclusion, and the project-level aggregate counts is correctly reasoned and documented in `source_caveats`.
